subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should normal source chats keep automatic bare-text delivery by default, or should OpenClaw move them to message-tool-only or final-only semantics to prevent inter-tool text leaks?
rationale: The remaining source-reproducible path is tied to an intentional compatibility boundary: current code and tests preserve automatic visible replies, but field reports show that boundary can expose internal assistant text.

options.title: Adopt safer delivery defaults
options.body: Make normal channel/source delivery message-tool-only or final-only by default with explicit migration or opt-out handling for users who rely on bare-text replies.

options.title: Keep automatic defaults
options.body: Preserve compatibility and rely on opt-in config or prompt discipline, accepting that customer-facing deployments must configure their own suppression.

options.title: Land opt-in mitigations first
options.body: Review the open fork PRs as escape hatches while keeping this canonical issue open for the default-policy decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt safer delivery defaults
recommendation.body: Make normal channel/source delivery message-tool-only or final-only by default with explicit migration or opt-out handling for users who rely on bare-text replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current evidence ties the delivery default policy to PR 83498, authored and merged by steipete.
